label: TSMM to HAVID experimental binding
description: Experimental binding that maps High Assurance Verifiable Identifier (HAVID) concepts into TSMM so composite identifier structures, assurance composition, lifecycle coordination, and revocation-aware verifier behavior can be compared without treating the current HAVID specification as a complete trust meta model.

mappings.description: Machine-verifiable composite trust artifact formed from cross-endorsed identifier surfaces whose validation result informs a relying decision.

mappings.externalConcept: Identifier class taxonomy (DID, DNS domain, X.509 certificate, LEI / organizational identifier)
mappings.description: Identifier classes are modeled as subject-bound identifier surfaces that contribute distinct assurance properties and should remain analytically separate even when cross-endorsed.
Bi-directional machine-readable linkage checked through native resolution mechanisms and used as the primary validation path for composite identifier trust.
Verifier-side interpretation of the combined assurance contributed by each identifier class, bounded by each identifier's native trust framework and integrity properties.
Structured verifier outcome describing whether the HAVID is fully validated, degraded, or invalid under current evidence and policy.
Operational rules governing renewal, update, synchronized key handling, expiry, and continued cross-endorsement maintenance across linked identifiers.
Reliance-changing operational consequence whereby a revoked, expired, or deactivated linked identifier invalidates the composite HAVID for verifier use.

notes: This is an experimental binding because the HAVID specification is still evolving and the TSMM mapping should be treated as provisional rather than canonical.
HAVID contributes a compositional identifier-assurance model. It does not replace verifier policy, delegated authority semantics, or broader trust-governance structures.
The binding is designed to keep identifier class, assurance contribution, lifecycle state, and revocation impact separable so downstream systems do not inflate cross-endorsement into blanket trust.

guarantees.name: identifier-class-separation
guarantees.description: Distinct identifier classes and their native assurance contributions can be modeled without collapsing them into one undifferentiated identifier claim.

guarantees.name: lifecycle-visible-composition
guarantees.description: Renewal, revocation, expiry, and re-establishment obligations can be represented as lifecycle-relevant policy and effect structures in TSMM.

guarantees.name: verifier-state-comparison
guarantees.description: HAVID validation states can be treated as assessment outputs that inform relying-party trust decisions.

guarantees.name: governance-completeness
guarantees.description: HAVID contributes high-assurance identifier composition, but broader authority, delegation, and ecosystem governance semantics remain outside the current specification.

limitations.name: no-native-authority-model
limitations.impact: A validated HAVID does not by itself describe what an identified party may do, under what mandate, or with what bounded authority.
limitations.mitigation: Compose HAVID-derived identity assurance with explicit delegation, authorization, and policy surfaces when consequential actions are in scope.

limitations.name: assurance-not-transferable
limitations.impact: Cross-endorsement does not cause one identifier class to inherit the native assurance of another identifier class.
limitations.mitigation: Keep per-identifier-class assurance contributions explicit in downstream profiles, evidence, and verifier logic.

limitations.name: spec-evolution-risk
limitations.impact: The HAVID specification is still under active development, so mapping details may need refresh as validation states, pairings, or extension rules evolve.
limitations.mitigation: Treat this binding as experimental and review it whenever the upstream HAVID specification changes materially.

behavioralExpectations.expectation: Verifiers treat HAVID as a composite identifier-assurance input that must still be interpreted under local policy and risk context.

Identifier controllers preserve or re-establish cross-endorsement links when linked identifiers are renewed, updated, or rotated, and verifiers downgrade reliance when linked state becomes stale, revoked, or expired.

notes: Binding remains subject to ecosystem-specific review and does not establish certification.
